existing_roles.title: Site Quality Director
existing_roles.description:
**Why Us?**

At Par Health, we believe great healthcare is built on getting the essentials right. We’re looking for passionate, talented individuals who share our commitment to improving lives. With a global workforce, we lead with pride and purpose—prioritizing quality and safety while fostering a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and teamwork. Elevating the Essentials isn’t just our tagline, it’s the higher standard we live by every day.

**Job Description Summary**

The Site Quality Director is responsible for ensuring cGMP compliance and product quality at the Raleigh, NC facility while supporting broader site quality initiatives aligned with company objectives. This role provides strategic leadership in the development, implementation, and oversight of the site quality systems to ensure that all manufacturing, testing, packaging, storage, and distribution activities meet regulatory standards and deliver the highest product quality. The Site Quality Director leads and mentors quality teams, oversees daily quality operations, and serves as a key partner to site leadership by providing guidance on quality and compliance across the organization.

**Job Description**

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* **Manages all aspects of Site Quality System including but not limited to: CAPA, exceptions, document management, complaint investigation handling, change control, supplier quality, OOS investigations, stability programs, and regulatory inspection readiness.**
* **Support a quality program which instils personal accountability for accuracy, consistency, and completeness for all operations**
* **Provides direction and leadership for the successful execution of quality activities, such as:**
* **Ensures health authority inspection (FDA, EU, Health Canada and others) readiness through development of compliance enhancement plans, internal audit program, and industry intelligence.**
* **Customer complaint investigation, including interaction with customers and resolution of critical issues.**
* **Manages the supplier quality program to fulfill regulatory and site needs.**
* **Conducts and/or administers new employee, ongoing, and directed training on GMP topics to ensure compliance to regulations. Manages site training compliance program.**
* **CAPA program to effectively identify and correct problems that impact product quality or compliance.**
* **Validation activities for new, altered, or modified equipment, facilities, or manufacturing processes.**
* **Customer audit process (approximately 50/yr.) to include preparation, hosting, and responding to issues noted – also, utilize input from customer audits and a continuous improvement tool.**
* **Documents management and label control to fulfill regulatory and business needs**
* **Stability program for both API products manufactured at the site.**
* **Approves highly technical investigations involving product impact.**
* **Sets direction and policies for cGMP compliance activities.**
* **Schedules employees through subordinates, performance appraisals, and performance management of team members.**
* **Budgets and adherence for areas of functional responsibility.**
* **Directly interacting with key customers relating to technical issues, potential non-compliance activities, or service issues impacted by quality/compliance.**
* **Resolution of critical quality issues that could impact production, customer service, quality, or compliance.**
* **Interprets regulatory guidance to determine site course of action for compliance.**
* **Technical expert in multiple quality functional areas, such as validation, product investigations, quality systems, and establishing compliance plans, etc.**

**DEPARTMENT** **SPECIFIC/NON-ESSENTIAL** **FUNCTIONS:**

* **Other duties as assigned with or without accommodation.**
* **Participates in a certified 5S Workplace System to ensure good housekeeping and organization.**

**MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:**

**Education:**

**BS Chemistry, Engineering, Life Science or related.**

**Experience:**

**7-10 years leadership experience in a chemical or pharmaceutical manufacturing environment, preferably specific to Quality and/or manufacturing related functions.**

**Preferred** **Skills/Qualifications:**

* **Working knowledge of chemical, pharmaceutical or bio-pharmaceutical manufacturing.**
* **Must have knowledge and understanding of applicable global regulations, GMP and compendial requirements.**
* **Must have thorough knowledge and understanding of QA regulations as they apply to this type of facility.**
* **Experience in driving improvements in quality systems and quality performance is preferred.**
* **Certification as a Six Sigma Black or Green Belt and/or as a Certified Quality Engineer is considered a plus.**
* **Must have high technical ability and excellent** **interpersonal/communication** **skills. Requires excellent oral and written skills and good negotiation skills to effectively communicate and influence the outcome of quality related plans, programs, and activities throughout the business unit.**
* **Must have the ability and experience to drive cost reduction while continuously improving performance, as well as the ability to lead employees in making these changes.**

**RELATIONSHIP WITH OTHERS/ SCOPE:**

* **This position reports to the Interim Head of Quality, Generics.**
* **This position will have frequent communication and working relationships with departments and plant managers.**
* **Interacts with internal Staff (Department and Plant Managers) on all Site management issues. Advises Staff on compliance issues. Report on overall performance and critical quality issues to Corporate Quality. Interacts with Corporate Quality personnel, R&D, and quality and managers within the organization. Works with Commercial team on customer issues. External contacts include regulatory authorities, state, federal and international (FDA, OSHA, EPA, NCDENR), suppliers, customers and community contacts.**
* **Financial responsibilities include managing multi-million payroll and operating budgets. Also recommends major purchases and capital expenditures that are necessary to maintain operations of QC laboratory and to maintain or improve the site’s GMP compliance and performance.**

**WORKING CONDITIONS:**

* **70% Office Environment**  
  **30% Laboratory and Plant environment including exposure to raw materials and finished products**
* **Must be willing and able to wear PPE including hard-hat, steel-toed shoes, safety glasses, and any other devices or equipment as specified for the position.**
* **Some travel is required, both domestically and internationally.**

**DISCLAIMER:**

**The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this** **classification.** **They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required of employees assigned to this position.**

**EEO Statement:**

We comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws prohibiting discrimination and harassment, and provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or genetic information, or any other classification protected by federal, state or local law. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation and training.

existing_roles.description:
Director-Quality Management - Acute | Highland Hospital | Charleston, West Virginia

**About the Job:**

PURPOSE STATEMENT:  
  
The Director of Quality, Risk & Compliance leads and coordinates quality and performance improvement, regulatory compliance, and patient safety efforts within the healthcare facility. This role ensures that all programs operate within local, state, federal, and accreditation standards, while driving a culture of continuous improvement, clinical excellence, and risk reduction.

**Roles and Responsibilities:**

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Provides oversight of all facility programs, including inpatient and outpatient services, ensuring alignment with quality, risk management, patient safety, and regulatory standards.
* Leads facility-wide quality, risk, and patient safety strategy and improvement efforts.
* Directs the Quality Assurance/Performance Improvement (QAPI) program, including development, implementation, and evaluation; monitors KPIs and ensures governance of data-driven improvement efforts.
* Drives organization-wide performance improvement initiatives through data analysis and system-level process enhancements to improve outcomes.
* Oversees incident reporting, investigations, and risk analyses (RCA/Event Analysis), ensuring timely resolution and prevention of recurrence.
* Maintains compliance with all local, state, federal (CMS), and accreditation standards (TJC), ensures ongoing survey readiness, and serves as the primary liaison during regulatory and accreditation surveys, audits, and required reporting activities.
* Partners with the Legal, Compliance, and Risk Department on high-risk events, complaints/allegations, investigations, and corrective action planning.
* Supports the development, review, and implementation of facility policies and procedures, ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements and consistent adherence across departments.
* Collaborates with department leaders and Human Resources to support staff accountability and ensure adherence to facility policies and procedures.
* Provides staff training and mentoring to support competency, accountability, and adherence to quality, risk, and safety standards, while fostering a culture of continuous improvement and patient safety.
* Conducts leadership rounding, medical record reviews, and monitoring of environment of care, safety, and documentation standards.
* Prepares and maintains required reports and documentation; participates in committees, meetings, audits, and organizational initiatives.
* Supervises Patient Advocate/Coordinator roles, when applicable, through hiring, orienting, performance assessment and management, motivating, training, scheduling, and coaching to meet department and facility goals. Supports resolution of patient concerns and patient rights processes.
* Serves as Patient Safety and Compliance Officer, providing oversight of patient safety, risk management, and event reporting processes within organizational governance structures.
* Serves as Patient Safety and Compliance Officer, providing oversight of client safety, risk management, and event reporting processes within organizational governance structures.
* May serve as Privacy/Security Officer, providing direction and oversight of activities related to compliance with applicable Federal and State law and regulations governing the privacy and security of health information.
* May serve as Chief Healthcare Disparities Officer, leading efforts to identify, analyze, and reduce disparities in care for the populations served.
* May be required to provide onsite coverage for other programs when needed, develops, and executes new programs according to market needs and may provide training, case consultation and Administrator On Call coverage during and after program hours as needed.

**EDUCATION/EXPERIENCE/SKILL REQUIREMENTS:**

* Bachelor’s degree with a clinical, nursing or business emphasis required. Master’s degree in Human Services preferred.
* Three years’ experience in quality, patient safety, regulatory compliance, risk management, survey management, behavioral health, substance use disorder treatment, or related experience required.
* Knowledge and understanding of state/federal regulations, Joint Commission and/or CARF Accreditation.

**LICENSES/DESIGNATIONS/CERTIFICATIONS:**

* CPHQ Preferred
* Professional clinical license issued by the appropriate licensing body as required by the state.
* CPR and de-escalation and restraint certification required (training available upon hire and offered by facility).
* First aid may be required based on state or facility

**WORK LOCATION:**

The Director of Quality is responsible for leading, designing, and continuously improving the organization's Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement (QAPI) program. This role ensures compliance with all federal, state, and accrediting body requirements while driving a culture of safety, accountability, and high-quality patient care. The Director of Quality partners closely with clinical, operational, and executive leadership to translate quality data into meaningful improvements that enhance patient outcomes, regulatory readiness, and organizational performance.

This leader serves as the organization's subject-matter expert on quality, survey preparedness, and performance improvement, balancing regulatory rigor with practical, frontline-focused solutions.

**Job Responsibilities**

* Lead and oversee the organization's QAPI program, ensuring alignment with CMS Conditions of Participation, state regulations, and accreditation standards.

* Develop, implement, and monitor performance improvement initiatives based on data trends, adverse events, and regulatory requirements.

**Regulatory Compliance & Survey Readiness**

* Serve as the primary owner of regulatory readiness, including CMS, state surveys, and accrediting body reviews.

* Oversee patient safety initiatives, including incident reporting, investigations, and follow-up actions.

* Lead root cause analyses (RCAs) and failure mode assessments as needed.

* Partner with clinical leadership to reduce risk, prevent harm, and improve safety outcomes for patients and staff.

**Data, Reporting & Insights**

* Develop and maintain quality dashboards and reports for executive leadership, agency leaders, and governing bodies.

* Translate complex quality and compliance data into clear, actionable insights.

* Ensure accurate and timely reporting of required quality measures and outcomes.

**Leadership, Education & Collaboration**

* Partner with Executive Directors, Clinical Leaders, and Medical Directors to embed quality expectations into daily operations.

* Educate and coach leaders and frontline staff on quality standards, best practices, and regulatory requirements.

* Support a culture of transparency, continuous learning, and accountability.

* Participate in leadership meetings and provide strategic guidance on quality-related decisions.

* Registered Nurse (RN) with active, unrestricted license

* Minimum 5 years of hospice or home health experience

* Minimum 3 years in quality, compliance, or clinical leadership

* Strong knowledge of CMS Hospice Conditions of Participation

* Experience with surveys and regulatory audits

* Strong analytical and communication skills

**Company Overview**

American Photonics, a portfolio company of BlueRock Global, is a precision optical manufacturer serving the aerospace, defense, industrial, medical, scientific, and commercial markets.

We are strengthening our manufacturing capabilities, investing in operational improvements, and expanding into higher-value precision optics and infrared applications.

We operate in a technically demanding manufacturing environment where quality, precision, accountability, and reliable execution are essential. Our focus is on building a stronger, more capable manufacturing business positioned for sustainable, profitable growth.

**Job Overview**

American Photonics is seeking an accomplished General Manager to lead overall business performance, manufacturing operations, and organizational development.

This is the senior on-site executive position, with direct responsibility for operating P&L performance and leadership across Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Sales, Supply Chain, and supporting business functions.

The ideal candidate has successfully led a technically complex manufacturing business, improved financial and operational results, developed accountable leadership teams, and executed meaningful business improvements.

We are looking for a decisive, hands-on leader who understands both the financial and operational sides of manufacturing. This individual must be equally comfortable reviewing business performance, resolving production challenges, developing customer relationships, and working directly with employees on the manufacturing floor.

Reporting to ownership, the General Manager will have responsibility for translating strategic objectives into achievable operating plans, establishing clear accountability, and delivering measurable results. The position will work closely with BlueRock's corporate resources while maintaining ownership of day-to-day business execution.

**Duties**

* Assume accountability for operating P&L performance, including revenue, gross margin, EBITDA, operating expenses, working capital, and achievement of financial objectives.

**Overview**

**At The Cheesecake Factory Bakery, We Don't Do Ordinary!** Nothing is scaled down. Not the pride, not the fun, and definitely not the teamwork. Here, you’ll have the opportunity to shape the future of our Bakery business, lead great people, and strengthen the systems behind the iconic cheesecakes our guests have loved for decades.

**As the VP, Quality Assurance & Food Safety**, you’ll report to the Bakery President and lead food safety, quality assurance, sanitation, and technical services across two bakery plants totaling more than 160,000 square feet and supporting more than 600 staff members. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact: setting the strategy, rebuilding organizational trust, strengthening audit readiness, and elevating Good Manufacturing Practices through disciplined root cause analysis and corrective action. You’ll operate at both the executive and plant levels, bringing the leadership, technical expertise, and influence needed to create lasting change.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **A Trusted Executive Leader:** You build credibility through transparency, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through, earning the confidence to influence decisions at every level.
* **A Strategic, Hands-On Quality Leader:** You set the vision while staying connected to operations, understanding risk, removing barriers, and translating strategy into consistent execution.
* **An Audit and Compliance Expert:** You build a culture of year-round readiness where issues are identified early, corrective actions are effective, and findings are sustainably closed.
* **A Disciplined Problem Solver:** You look beyond the immediate issue, using data, risk assessment, and root cause analysis to solve systemic problems and prevent recurrence.

**Responsibilities**

* Set and lead the Bakery division’s Quality Assurance and Food Safety strategy across both facilities, establishing clear expectations for risk management, performance, and accountability.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to the Bakery President and executive leadership, providing clear perspective on food safety and quality risks, audit readiness, significant incidents, and corrective actions.
* Ensure trust and confidence in the function through technical credibility, transparency, strong partnerships, and consistent execution.

* Ensure highly systematic and disciplined adherence to product and process standards on a real-time basis to guarantee our cakes are beautiful and delicious.
* Build greater rigor around root cause analysis and corrective and preventive actions, addressing systemic issues rather than symptoms.
* Provide leadership across product and process quality, customer complaints, foreign-material controls, product holds, specifications, labeling, formulas, recipes, and Technical Services.
* Establish meaningful metrics and use data to identify trends, prioritize risk, and hold the organization accountable for results.
* Lead significant food safety, quality, sanitation, and regulatory matters with urgency, sound judgment, and appropriate escalation.
* Build and develop a high-performing Quality Assurance, Food Safety, Sanitation, and Technical Services organization with the talent and capabilities needed for long-term success.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Research and Development, and Human Resources to strengthen ownership and accountability for food safety and quality across the business.
* Prioritize resources and investments against the greatest risks and opportunities while effectively managing the function’s budget.

* Expertise in root cause analysis, corrective and preventive action, risk assessment, and incident investigation.

* Leadership experience within the bakery or dessert industry; experience in similarly complex food-manufacturing environments will also be considered.

About Us

  

Skydweller Aero Inc. is a transatlantic, cutting-edge aerospace company developing solar-powered aircraft solutions capable of perpetual flight while carrying heavy and powerful payloads. Building on technology from the longest continuous renewably powered flight program in history, this fast-growing company is creating a new class of unmanned aircraft. It combines the persistence of geosynchronous satellites with the sensing capabilities and flexibility of a large airborne platform. Skydweller Aero Inc. has its global and US headquarters in Oklahoma City, with European operations headquartered in Spain.

Role Summary

  

As Skydweller prepares to move from development toward aircraft production, we are looking for an experienced manufacturing executive to build and lead our production organization. This role is based in **Oklahoma City, OK** and reports to the Chief Operating Officer.

The Vice President, Manufacturing & Production will own all aircraft production operations: final assembly, systems integration, avionics installation, production testing, factory operations and aircraft delivery. You will lead the organization as we scale from prototype and low-rate initial production into sustained manufacturing.

We are looking for a hands-on aerospace manufacturing leader with a proven track record of building production organizations, improving factory performance and delivering complex aircraft in FAA-regulated environments.

**Why join:** Most manufacturing leadership roles optimize an existing production system. This one builds it. You will establish the manufacturing organization, develop the factory workforce, and scale production of one of the most ambitious autonomous aircraft programs in aerospace.

Responsibilities

  

**Production leadership**

  

* Lead all aircraft production and manufacturing operations.
* Drive safe, efficient and repeatable aircraft production.
* Build and lead a high-performing manufacturing organization, with clear management systems, metrics and operating rhythms.
* Foster a culture of accountability, safety, quality and continuous improvement.

  

**Assembly and integration**

* Oversee final assembly, systems and electrical integration, avionics installation and aircraft completion.
* Ensure aircraft are built to engineering, quality and regulatory requirements.
* Drive production readiness and resolve manufacturing constraints and bottlenecks.

  

**Production planning and execution**

* Own execution of the Master Production Schedule.
* Lead production planning, labor allocation and resource management.
* Set capacity plans that support production-rate growth.
* Monitor factory performance and drive throughput, productivity and efficiency improvements.

  

**Production testing and acceptance**

existing_roles.description:
ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL — we're the tech-powered growth partner for ecommerce brands, running 12+ owned fulfillment centers across the US, Canada, the UK, and Europe so our merchants can stress less and grow more.

We are seeking a hands-on Director to join our Strategy & Operations team and lead high-impact initiatives that improve how ShipMonk works across departments. Reporting to our Senior Director of Strategy and Operations, you will take our most important cross-functional problems from a blank page to a deployed solution: framing the problem, defining success, building the answer, and proving the results. Your first major initiative will be transforming how we schedule, staff, and manage our hourly warehouse workforce.  
  
What you'll do:  
  
Lead Cross-Department Initiatives

* Lead major initiatives that improve processes across departments, especially where work, systems, and ownership break down between teams.
* Frame ambiguous problems, define the outcome, and work backward into a solution that teams actually adopt.
* Lead on-site discovery with leaders and frontline teams to understand how work really gets done.

Transform Workforce Management

* Lead the redesign of how we schedule, staff, and manage our hourly warehouse teams, starting from what the business needs to achieve.
* Pilot solutions in one fulfillment center and scale what works across our network.
* Track the outcomes that matter, such as labor cost, staffing coverage, and retention.

Drive Continuous Improvement

* Help the whole organization work better, improving quality, speed, and the employee and merchant experience, not just cost.
* Spot recurring friction across teams, prioritize the biggest opportunities, and help teams adopt improvements that last.
* Make structured problem solving a habit at every level of the organization.

Strengthen Our Governance

* Support the organization as it matures how it sets priorities, makes decisions, and follows through on commitments.
* Partner with leaders to build governance practices that fit how each team works rather than imposing one structure.
* Bring clear analysis and decision materials to executive discussions.

Analyze, Build, and Drive Adoption

* Analyze productivity, capacity, cost to serve, and profitability, and build models that quantify trade-offs and turn decisions into action.
* Prototype tools and workflows hands-on with AI tools such as Claude, and partner with Engineering and Data to take them to production.
* Spend meaningful time on-site, leading change management so improvements stick rather than fade after launch.

What you'll need:

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, business, supply chain, or a related field
* 3-5 years of experience in operations transformation, strategy, or management consulting, including leading implementations from requirements through deployment and adoption
* A track record of solving ambiguous, cross-functional problems with structured, KPI-driven thinking
* Experience leading process redesign and change management across departments; Lean, Six Sigma, or similar experience is a plus
* Strong analytical and financial modeling skills; SQL or BI experience is a plus
* A hands-on ownership style: comfortable on the warehouse floor and personally driving execution and adoption
* Experience building with AI tools such as Claude to prototype solutions
* Exposure to fulfillment, distribution, or manufacturing operations; workforce management experience is a plus
* Strong executive communication and the ability to influence without direct authority
* Ability to travel 25–35%, with more time on-site during discovery and rollouts

**About ShipMonk**

ShipMonk isn't just a 3PL; we're a **growth partner for merchants**. We provide cutting-edge technology and a network of owned and operated fulfillment centers that empower high-growth ecommerce and DTC brands to stress less and grow more. With over 2,500 employees across five countries, we're on a mission to revolutionize fulfillment by providing everything from the fastest click-to-delivery and real-time inventory to custom solutions—all with a **merchant**-**first** mindset.

**Why ShipMonk?**

We believe in building for the long term, and our success is powered by five key differentiators that help us become true partners to our merchants.

* **Global Fulfillment Network:** Our 12+ owned and operated fulfillment centers span the US, Canada, the U.K., and Mainland Europe. We never outsource, ensuring quality and consistency.  
  + **Proprietary Technology:** We've eliminated the need for tribal knowledge with our AI-powered platform. It provides a real-time, unified view of inventory and orders, giving our merchants the control and visibility they need to succeed.
  + **Unrivaled Support:** We provide hands-on, "mom and pop" support with a global reach. Our dedicated teams are on-site at every fulfillment center, ready to jump into action.
  + **Transparent Pricing**: We believe in honest, long-term partnerships. Our all- inclusive pricing means predictable costs, with no hidden fees or surprises.
  + **Committed to the Future:** We invest over $10 million annually in research and development to ensure our technology and services continually evolve, helping merchants plant roots with a partner who is here to stay.

**Our Core Values**

Our values are the heart of our culture. We're looking for individuals who embody these principles every day.

* **Merchant-first:** We handle the logistics so our merchants can focus on what they do best—growing their business.
* **People make ShipMonk:** We believe in our team and invest in our people.
* **Own it:** We take ownership of our work, our mistakes, and our successes.
* **Get sh\*t done:** We're a fast-paced, high-growth company that values action and results.
* **Change the score:** We challenge the status quo, constantly innovating and improving.

  

ShipMonk is an equal opportunity employer. We value diversity and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

* **Full Site Ownership**

o Own end-to end performance of the Tulsa site across safety, quality, delivery, and cost.

o Establish clear accountability and performance standards across all functions.

o Act as the **site leader**, setting expectations, pace, and operating discipline.

* **Build + Scale the Operation**

o Build structure, process discipline, and management routines that drive consistency and predictability.

o Drive labor productivity and cost efficiency across the site.

* **Supply Chain & Material Flow Excellence**

o Improve material availability, planning accuracy, and supplier coordination.

o Optimize inventory levels, accuracy, and working capital performance.

o Lead warehouse operations to ensure efficient flow from receiving through shipping.

* **Continuous Improvement with Measurable Impact**

o Lead Industrial Engineering and Continuous Improvement as core drivers of performance.

o Implement Lean principles focused on outcomes – not activity.

o Establish structured problem-solving and root cause discipline.

o Reduce cost of poor quality (COPQ), including scrap, rework, and inefficiencies.

* **Leadership & Team Transformation**

o Build and lead a high-performance leadership team across all functions.

o Upgrade talent where needed and develop strong internal capability.

o Create a culture of accountability, urgency, and execution.

o Develop succession plans and leadership depth to support continued scale.

* **Cross-Functional Integration**

o Partner with Engineering to ensure manufacturability and smooth new product introduction.

o Align closely with Supply Chain and Commercial teams to match production with demand.

o Ensure operational commitments are realistic, executable, and consistently delivered.

* **Safety & Quality Leadership**

o Champion a safety-first culture with zero tolerance for shortcuts.

o Drive improvements in quality, process capability, and consistency.

o Ensure robust systems are in place and followed across the operation.

  

**Hayden Industrial has determined this position involves safety-sensitive job duties and will be considered a safety-sensitive position for purpose of the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana and Patient Protection Act (“The Unity Bill.”) effective August 29th, 2019.**

**Education and Experience:**

* Bachelors degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or Supply Chain

* 12 – 20 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.

* Proven track record leading **large, complex manufacturing operations (approaching or exceeding $100M in scale).**

* Experience with full site ownership including **manufacturing, supply chain, and warehouse operations.**

Director of Operations, North America

**About Us:**

We are committed to finding smart solutions that enable an intelligent and seamless world. Our success as a world-class leader in technology has evolved from humble beginnings. In 1896, the enterprising father and son team of A.J. and George A. Briggs partnered with S.A. Buffington, a Chicago lawyer, to establish Chicago Telephone Supply Company (later to become CTS).

Today, CTS is a leading designer and manufacturer of sensors, actuators, and electronic components for suppliers and original equipment manufacturers. We have over 20 locations in 12 countries and more than 3,500 employees. Our innovative sensing, connectivity, and motion solutions offer a diverse range of products across diversified end markets including transportation, medical, aerospace and defense, and industrial. We are at the forefront of supporting innovating life-changing technology, focusing on quality to keep people safe, healthy, and happy.

**Position Summary**

The Operations Director, North America provides strategic and operational leadership for the regional manufacturing network, ensuring safe, compliant, cost-effective, and customer-focused execution across assigned sites. This position requires a hands-on, execution-focused leader who can standardize operating processes, improve performance variability across sites, coach plant leadership teams, and convert strategic business priorities into measurable operational and financial results. This role is accountable for safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, customer responsiveness, capital execution, and people development across the North America plants.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead the North America manufacturing operations network, establishing clear priorities, standard work, operating cadences, and performance expectations across assigned sites.
* Own regional operational performance and operational excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, inventory, productivity, customer responsiveness, and employee engagement metrics.
* Partner with business unit leadership, plant managers, supply chain, quality, engineering, finance, HR, and commercial teams to align operating plans with customer demand and business objectives.
* Establish and reinforce standardized operating processes across the region while allowing appropriate site-level flexibility based on product, customer, and regulatory requirements.
* Drive a disciplined daily, weekly, and monthly management system to review performance, identify gaps, assign accountability, and ensure timely corrective actions.
* Translate operational actions into financial outcomes by improving margin performance, controlling costs, optimizing resources, and partnering with finance on budgeting and forecasting.
* Provide leadership, coaching, and development for plant managers and site leadership teams, building a strong succession pipeline and culture of accountability.

* Reduce performance variability between sites by deploying common metrics, operating reviews, best-practice sharing, and targeted improvement plans.

* Support digital manufacturing, automation, data transparency, and ERP-enabled process improvements where they improve operational control, productivity, and decision-making.

* Establish strong communication routines with site and regional teams to reinforce priorities, escalate risks, and ensure alignment on business-critical actions.
* Ensure compliance with corporate policies, business unit procedures, internal controls, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

**Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities**

* Strong multi-site manufacturing leadership experience with demonstrated ability to deliver results through plant leadership teams.
* Deep knowledge of Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, structured problem solving, visual management, standard work, and daily management systems.
* Strong business acumen, including budgeting, forecasting, P&L management, productivity analysis, labor planning, capital investment justification, and margin improvement.
* Demonstrated ability to standardize processes across sites while adapting execution to local operating realities and customer requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through influence across operations, supply chain, quality, engineering, finance, HR, and commercial functions.
* Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to engage shop-floor teams, plant leadership, executives, and customers.
* Ability to prioritize competing objectives, manage risk, lead through change, and make timely decisions in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
* Proven track record of building high-performing teams, developing leaders, improving retention, and creating succession plans for critical operations roles.
* High integrity, sound judgment, and commitment to safety, quality, compliance, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business Administration, or a related field required; master’s degree or MBA preferred.
* Minimum of 12 to 15 years of progressive manufacturing operations experience, including leadership of complex plant operations.
* Minimum of 5 years of multi-site operations leadership experience preferred, with accountability for regional performance across multiple plants or business units.
* Experience leading manufacturing operations in North America, including cross-border or multi-country operating environments, preferred.
* Experience with P&L ownership, operating budgets, capital planning, productivity programs, operational KPI management, and financial performance improvement required.
* Demonstrated experience with Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or equivalent continuous improvement systems required; certification preferred.
* Experience with ERP systems, manufacturing data, automation initiatives, and digital operations tools preferred.
* Experience in automotive, electronics, sensors, mechatronics, industrial manufacturing, or similarly regulated manufacturing environments preferred.
* Bilingual English/Spanish capability preferred, particularly for roles supporting Mexico operations.

**Physical Demands**

* Must follow applicable safety requirements while visiting manufacturing areas, including use of required personal protective equipment.
* Ability to work several hours at a computer and participate in meetings across multiple time zones.

**Senior Manager of Operations**

**Scottsdale Mint | Casper, Wyoming**  
**Employment Type:** Full-Time | Salaried

**Company Summary**

Founded in 2008, Scottsdale Mint is a U.S.-based precious metals manufacturer recognized globally for its innovation, quality, and American craftsmanship. As a privately held producer of premium gold, silver, and platinum bullion, the company serves sovereign nations, central banks, Fortune 500 companies, industrial clients, and authorized distributors worldwide.

Operating from its advanced manufacturing facility in Casper, Wyoming, Scottsdale Mint specializes in high-purity bullion, legal-tender coin programs, and custom-branded precious metal products. The company combines artistic design, scientific precision, and advanced minting technology to deliver products recognized for their quality, detail, and authenticity.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Manager of Operations is responsible for overseeing the daily performance and overall effectiveness of Scottsdale Mint's Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing departments. This position provides leadership and direction to approximately 30 employees, ensuring manufacturing operations are safe, efficient, productive, and aligned with company objectives.

The successful candidate will be a visible, hands-on leader capable of managing multiple manufacturing functions, developing departmental supervisors, establishing accountability, and improving operational performance while supporting current production requirements and future manufacturing growth.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Manufacturing & Operations Management**

* Oversee daily operations and production performance across Coining, Melting, CNC Machining, and Die Manufacturing.
* Establish departmental priorities, production goals, and performance expectations in coordination with senior management.
* Coordinate labor, equipment, and resources to maximize productivity, throughput, and manufacturing capacity.
* Monitor production schedules and workflow, identifying bottlenecks and implementing solutions to improve output and efficiency.
* Coordinate with Planning & Inventory Control, Fulfillment, Maintenance, Marketing, and other departments to support production requirements and company objectives.
* Develop, monitor, and report on departmental KPIs to optimize workforce utilization and ensure production schedule adherence.

**2. Leadership & Workforce Management**

* Provide leadership, direction, and accountability to departmental supervisors and employees.
* Manage staffing levels, scheduling, attendance, and labor allocation to meet production requirements.
* Establish clear expectations for employee performance, productivity, communication, and workplace conduct.
* Conduct performance reviews, address personnel matters, and establish development objectives for direct reports.
* Develop supervisory capabilities and ensure employees receive appropriate training to perform their responsibilities effectively.
* Foster a professional work environment emphasizing teamwork, accountability, ownership, and employee development.

**3. Safety, Compliance & Operational Excellence**

* Maintain consistent operating standards, manufacturing procedures, and a strong safety culture across all assigned departments.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA regulations, company safety policies, and applicable workplace requirements.
* Monitor key performance indicators, including production output, labor efficiency, downtime, quality, and schedule attainment.
* Evaluate manufacturing processes to identify safety concerns, operational inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.
* Promote proper equipment operation, preventative maintenance, housekeeping, and organization throughout manufacturing areas.
* Ensure operational and safety issues are addressed promptly and corrective actions are implemented.
* Communicate departmental performance, challenges, and improvement initiatives to senior management.

**Qualifications & Experience**

* 5–7 years of progressive manufacturing supervisory or management experience, preferably overseeing multiple departments.
* Experience managing production teams and workforces of approximately 25–50 employees preferred.
* Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Operations Management, or a related discipline preferred; equivalent practical experience will be considered.
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production workflows, labor management, and operational efficiency.
* Working knowledge of OSHA regulations and manufacturing safety requirements.
* Demonstrated ability to manage production objectives, develop supervisors, and hold employees accountable for performance.
* Strong organizational, problem-solving, and verbal and written communication skills.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and manufacturing-related reporting systems.

**Position Expectations**

The Senior Manager of Operations is expected to take ownership of the overall performance of the assigned manufacturing departments. This individual must provide consistent leadership, establish clear priorities, and ensure departmental supervisors are effectively managing their teams and achieving established objectives.

Success will be measured by the ability to meet production goals, maintain safe and efficient operations, effectively manage workforce resources, improve manufacturing performance, and develop a capable and accountable team.

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee discount
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Paid time off
* Referral program
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Why work at Chromalloy?
  
Chromalloy employees are proud, passionate problem-solvers who strive to live our values every day. A career with Chromalloy is an opportunity to learn from top industry experts, work with important technologies, and unlock a passion for innovation. Join our team of experts, innovators and problem-solvers delivering world-class solutions for our customers. This role provides leadership, direction, and coaching to ensure business goals are achieved while maintaining a strong focus on safety, quality, customer service, operational excellence, and employee development.
  
  
The successful candidate will lead the full Quality organization — Quality Engineers, Quality Supervisors, Lab Technicians (Cal & Met Lab), NDT, Compliance, and Inspectors — while directing quality systems, driving regulatory compliance, and fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  
  
Work That Matters
  
At Chromalloy, your work directly supports aviation safety and reliability. Our teams repair and manufacture critical aerospace components used across the global aviation industry. As a people leader, you'll play a key role in developing talent, improving processes, and delivering results that help keep aircraft flying safely around the world.
  
  
**Location:** San Diego, CA
  
**Travel:** Occasional travel required
  
**Schedule:** On-site
  
  
What You’ll Be Doing
  

* Lead, coach, and develop a multi-level Quality organization including Quality Engineers, Supervisors, Compliance, NDT, Laboratory Operations, and Inspection teams.
* Establish quality objectives, policies, and performance expectations that drive accountability and continuous improvement.
* Own and continually improve the site's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with AS9100, FAA, EASA, CAAC, and customer requirements.
* Lead internal audits, corrective action programs, escape management investigations, and root cause analysis efforts.

* Lead customer and regulatory interactions, audits, and quality reviews.

* Analyze quality metrics and trends to identify risks, drive improvements, and support data-driven decision-making.

What We’re Looking For

* Strong knowledge of AS9100 and aerospace regulatory requirements, including FAA, EASA, and CAAC.
* Proven experience driving organizational performance, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Expertise in root cause analysis, corrective action systems, and quality management principles.
* Experience leading cross-functional projects within complex manufacturing or MRO environments.
* Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills

Nice to Have
  

* Advanced degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field
* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Six Sigma Black Belt, or similar certification
* Proven leadership experience in multi-site aerospace manufacturing or MRO operations
* Bilingual English and Spanish proficiency
* Experience implementing advanced inspection technologies, automation, or digital quality systems
* Experience developing and monitoring complex project budgets, resource needs, and timelines

Leadership Expectations and Values
  

* Sets Direction: Aligns people and decisions to Chromalloy’s vision and delivers results through transparency and accountability.
* Business Leadership: Drives enterprise value through sound judgment, cross-functional collaboration, and customer focus.
* Leads with Courage: Communicates openly, addresses challenges directly, and fosters accountability.
* Acts Decisively: Makes informed decisions, empowers others, and drives continuous improvement.
* Builds Talent: Develops diverse, high-performing teams through trust, respect, and inclusion.
* Owns Results: Sets clear expectations, establishes standards, and delivers operational excellence.

This position may require work hours outside of the regularly scheduled hours to meet operational needs. This may include work during evenings, weekends, and/or holidays. Additional work hours are assigned based on business requirements. Non-exempt employees will be paid overtime in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.
  
The salary range for this position reflects a broad spectrum of experience levels. Individual compensation within the range is determined by multiple factors, including relevant experience, education, certifications, job related skills, internal equity, and market conditions. existing_roles.title: Director of Fund Operations
existing_roles.description:
**Director, Fund Operations**

**POSITION:** Full-time Exempt

**DEPARTMENT:** Impact Investing

**REPORTS TO:** Vice President, Impact Investing

**About the Organization**

**A FOUNDATION BUILT ON GREATER ATLANTA’S FUTURE**

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta is one of the nation’s largest community foundations, with over $1.7 billion in assets and more than seven decades of philanthropic leadership. Through grants, donor services, civic partnerships and impact investments, CFGA advances equity and opportunity across 23 counties in the Greater Atlanta region.

**The Role**

**BUILDING THE OPERATING FOUNDATION FOR IMPACT INVESTING**

The Director of Fund Operations will provide strategic and operational leadership for the organization’s impact investing fund platform. This role is responsible for strengthening and scaling the systems, processes, infrastructure, and controls necessary to support a growing and sophisticated investment portfolio. This person owns the end-to-end operating model for the Foundation's impact investment platform. This is a senior, hands-on role responsible for making sure that once an investment is approved, it closes, funds, is serviced and is reported on correctly, on time and with a clear record. The work spans closing, funding, servicing, fund administration, compliance, records, data and reporting. This role supports every fund and vehicle on the platform — including the GoATL Community Capacity Fund, GoATL Affordable Housing Fund, TogetherATL Affordable Housing Fund, GoATL Community Guarantee Pool, and the Atlanta Affordable Housing Fund — together with related joint ventures and special purpose entities.

In practice, this person is the platform’s operational backbone: the person who knows what each transaction and fund requires, organizes the people and documents needed to satisfy those requirements, maintains the authoritative record, anticipates deadlines and exceptions, and follows issues through to resolution. The Director does not practice law or make accounting or credit decisions. Instead, the role makes sure Legal, Finance and the investment team work together smoothly and that nothing falls through the cracks.

The Director works hand in hand with the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing, who sits in Finance. The Director owns the process and the operating record: deadlines, checklists, documents, vendor performance and the loan database. The Fund Accountant owns the books: the general ledger, fund financial statements, capital accounts, investor statements and audit work. The Director makes sure the right information arrives complete and on time; the Fund Accountant decides how it is recorded and signs off on the numbers.

The successful candidate will combine transaction discipline, financial fluency, legal-document literacy, systems thinking and persistent follow-through. This person must be comfortable moving between a closing checklist, a fund agreement, a late borrower report, a wire request, a reporting calendar and a vendor escalation without losing track of what the governing documents require or the record of what was done.

**Why This Role Matters**

The platform now manages more than 60 loans across multiple funds and vehicles and is preparing to deploy its next round of capital. It has outgrown a model in which staff fill each operational gap as it appears. This role will connect the investment team, Finance, Legal and outside providers into one way of working: smooth closings, consistent records, clear deadlines, and systems that hold what we know about each fund, relationship and investment, so that knowledge does not live only in people’s heads.

* Creates one accountable owner for the transaction and fund lifecycle after investment approval.
* Replaces informal handoffs and institutional memory with documented workflows, complete records, calendars, controls and escalation paths.
* Gives Finance (including the Fund Accountant, Impact Investing), Legal and Portfolio Management a disciplined operating counterpart while preserving their independent authority.
* Ensures outside administrators, servicers and specialists work as extensions of our own process, with the Foundation keeping ownership of its records and decisions.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

**WHAT YOU’LL DO**

**Transaction Closing and Funding Coordination**

* Own the closing process from approval through funding and loan setup with the servicer, maintaining a complete checklist of approval conditions, legal documents, due diligence, signatures, funding mechanics and post-closing items. Because real estate deals fund on the day of closing, every item, including the wire request, must be ready before signing day.
* Translate investment approvals and term sheets into coordinated workplans for the deal lead, Legal, Finance and the Fund Accountant, Treasury, the borrower and outside providers; surface conflicts, gaps and sequencing issues early.
* Coordinate document production and review, signature processes, lien and lender-agreement requirements, organizational documents, insurance, required consents and other closing deliverables. Track legal questions to formal resolution by counsel.
* Confirm that every funding and wire request is complete before it goes to Finance or Treasury: required approvals are in place, the borrower’s wire instructions have been verified by a phone call, and two people are involved in every wire. Maintain the standard wire request form used for both closings and construction draws.
* Ensure each closed transaction is set up accurately and handed off to the assigned portfolio owner with final documents, payment terms, covenants, reporting obligations, draw requirements and key dates recorded in the system of record under the loan’s ID.
* Give the Fund Accountant the final executed terms, funded amounts and key dates for each closing, so the loan is set up in the books from the same record.

**Fund and Entity Operations**

* Manage operating calendars and workflows for each fund, entity and capital source, including capital calls, distributions, investor onboarding, bank account administration (account openings and authorized signers), subscriptions, side letters, governance actions and record retention. The Fund Accountant calculates investor allocations, capital accounts and distribution amounts and records them; this role runs the calendar, notices and documents around them.
* Own a single, current investor contact list, including financial advisors and fund administrator portal access, so that capital call notices, reports and distributions reach the right people.
* Maintain one register of what each fund is required to do under its governing agreements, side letters, policies, approval authorities and committee actions; coordinate implementation with the accountable business, Legal and Finance owners.
* Track state filings, annual report deadlines and registered-agent requirements across all entities, and support General Counsel as needed in preparing and completing these filings. General Counsel owns legal and state filings and Finance owns tax and regulatory filings; this role keeps one shared calendar for all of them.
* Support cash forecasting and liquidity planning by giving the Fund Accountant and the Vice President, Impact Investing expected closing, draw and repayment dates, while preserving Finance's authority over cash, treasury policy and accounting treatment.
* Support Finance-led annual audits and tax work by gathering key information and answering common requests. The Fund Accountant manages the audit and the auditor relationship, and Finance keeps ownership of audit and tax strategy, filings and sign-off. Organize valuations and other fund-level deliverables by assembling source materials, tracking deadlines, coordinating responses and driving open items to resolution.

**Servicing and Portfolio Operations**

* Own the operational relationship with loan servicers and administrators, including billing, payment processing, notices, escrows, statements, payoff calculations, deadline reminders and follow-up on exceptions.
* Ensure payments, draws, amendments, waivers, modifications and payoff activity are documented, routed and recorded consistently. Escalate issues that stay unresolved and any service failures.
* Run the quarterly borrower reporting process: track whether each report has arrived and is complete, send notices when reports are late or missing pieces, and make sure reviewed figures are recorded in the system of record.
* Keep the calendar for annual affordability compliance reviews (rents, incomes and other terms required by each loan’s affordability restrictions) and loan maturities, so reviews by asset managers happen on schedule.
* Coordinate operational support for loans in workout or needing special attention, including document collection, approval tracking, counsel coordination and implementation of authorized actions.
* Distinguish operational monitoring from credit judgment: route substantive covenant, borrower-performance and risk matters to Portfolio and Asset Management and track resulting actions to completion.

**Data, Records and Reporting Infrastructure**

* Carry out the platform’s plan to move from scattered files and systems (including Foundant, SharePoint, Excel, the DocuSign data room, and the fund administrator’s Egnyte and Salesforce portal) to a single system of record, working with Investment, Finance, Legal, IT and the fund administrator.
* In coordination with IT and third-party partners, establish and maintain the system of record (a loan database) for fund, investor and transaction information, with clear ownership, access controls, shared IDs, naming standards and a full history of changes. Key terms lock at closing and change only through a dated, approved modification.
* Work with IT to build and maintain automated workflows (for example, in Power Automate) that move data between systems, send deadline alerts and refresh Power BI dashboards, and use AI tools to prepare summaries and checks for staff to review. Coordinate with the Fund Accountant so the loan database and the accounting records tie out.
* Own operational data quality and check that key fields match across closing records, servicing systems, administrator records and Finance systems; resolve any differences with the appropriate source owner.
* Maintain the master calendar for investor reporting, committee, board, audit, tax, compliance and portfolio deliverables and coordinate timely inputs from accountable content owners.

**Vendor Management and Process Improvement**

* Serve as the primary business owner for third-party fund administration, servicing, payment processing and related operational providers; set service standards, make sure the Foundation has access to the source records, and define how issues are escalated and when a provider can be replaced.
* Share vendor oversight with the Fund Accountant: this role owns the relationship, contract terms, service standards and timeliness; the Fund Accountant reviews the financial accuracy of what providers produce (interest, balances, investor statements and fund reports) before it is posted or shared.
* Monitor service performance, check that provider reports arrive on time and match the operating record (the Fund Accountant checks the financial figures) and lead resolution of errors, backlogs and control failures.
* Document and continuously improve workflows for approvals, closings, disbursements, servicing, amendments, reporting and record retention. Partner with the Fund Accountant where workflows touch the books, such as the monthly close; Finance owns accounting procedures and reconciliations.
* Design procedures that are durable, teachable and appropriately scaled rather than dependent on one employee's memory or heroics.

**Team Leadership and Coordination**

* Manage any future operations or servicing staff; establish clear ownership, service expectations and backup coverage.
* Run recurring operating meetings that convert cross-functional issues into decisions, named owners and deadlines.
* Refine roles, responsibilities, workflows, and accountability standards across teams involved in fund operations and investment management.
* Raise issues promptly and concisely with the Vice President, Impact Investing and enterprise leadership (legal and finance) when service failures, unresolved legal or financial questions, capacity constraints or control gaps threaten a closing, obligation or relationship.
* Build strong working relationships across teams while being willing to insist on complete documentation, clear authority and timely decisions.

**Qualifications**  
**WHAT YOU BRING**

**Required**

* Five or more years of progressively responsible experience in fund operations, transaction management, loan administration, investment operations, structured finance, real estate finance, private credit, community development finance or a closely related field.
* Bachelor's degree in finance, accounting, business, real estate, public administration or a related field required.
* Demonstrated experience coordinating transactions through closing and funding, including legal documentation, cash mechanics and post-closing requirements.
* Working knowledge of financial statements, loan and investment documents, entity and fund records, payment and servicing processes, reconciliations and internal controls.
* Ability to build, lead, and evolve operational functions within a growing or complex organization.
* Confidence in evaluating existing practices, constructively challenging the status quo, and driving meaningful process improvements.
* Exceptional project management and organizational judgment, with the ability to maintain accuracy across multiple vehicles, transactions, deadlines and stakeholders.
* Strong written communication and the ability to convert complex requirements into clear checklists, procedures, records and short, clear updates for leadership when something is off track.
* Experience holding internal and external partners accountable, escalating appropriately and following issues through closure.
* A clear commitment to CFGA’s mission of equity and shared prosperity for all.

**Preferred**

* Experience with affordable housing, community development lending, program-related investments, impact investing or philanthropic investment vehicles.
* Experience managing a third-party fund administrator, loan servicer, closing counsel, tax provider or comparable outsourced operating partner.
* Experience building or improving an operating model, system of record, compliance calendar or reporting infrastructure.
* Comfort with Microsoft 365 tools such as SharePoint, Lists, Power Automate and Power BI; loan or relationship management systems such as Foundant or Salesforce; and tools used to summarize and check documents.
* Masters degree in relevant field.
* Relevant legal-operations, paralegal, fund-administration or project-management training is valuable; a law degree or CPA is not required.

**HYBRID SCHEDULE**

The Community Foundation operates in a hybrid working environment with staff working in-office three days per week and the opportunity to work two days remotely per week if in good standing.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

Compensation will be determined based on experience and qualifications. The salary range is

$130,000 - $150,000. This position is exempt and eligible for the Foundation’s competitive health and benefits plan, which includes:

**Paid time off**

* Four weeks accrued paid vacation
* Two weeks accrued paid sick leave
* Four mental health days
* Two personal days
* Two floating holidays
* Ten holidays

**Benefits**

* All benefits effective on date of hire with no waiting period
* 100% employer-paid medical, dental and vision coverage for employee-only plans
* 100% employer-paid life insurance, AD&D, short-term disability and long-term disability
* 100% employer-paid downtown Atlanta parking or monthly MARTA card
* Affordable plans for legal insurance, critical illness, supplemental life and more
* Immediate eligibility to contribute to a 403(b), plus a 6% employer-paid contribution after one year regardless of employee contributions
* Cell phone stipend
* Employee Donor Advised Fund after one year
* Employee Assistance Program and more

**Culture, Learning & Development**

* Individual Development Plans with training, resources and development opportunities
* Two wellness rooms with self-care resources
* Monthly employee engagement activities

**TO APPLY**

Submit your resume and cover letter through our Careers website.

Note: Only applications submitted through our website will be accepted. Due to the volume of candidates, we are unable to provide status updates or accommodate phone calls or walk-ins regarding open positions.

The Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

Community Foundation for Greater Atlanta values diversity and inclusion; we honor the diverse needs, strengths, voices and backgrounds of all individuals in our regional community.

We are seeking an exceptionally skilled Director of Service Operations Trade Compliance Operations to lead our world-class trade compliance operations across our global service supply chain. This is an outstanding opportunity to ensure that service parts, replacement systems, and returned products move across borders flawlessly while supporting our customer and factory commitments.

  

This role is key to the daily management and continuous refinement of trade compliance related to return material authorization (RMA), repair, replacement, refurbishment, and service inventory movements. You’ll partner with Legal, Global Trade, Service Planning, Logistics, warehouse teams, and service providers to convert requirements into clear, reliable processes.

  

**What you’ll be doing:**

* Lead trade compliance execution across service fulfillment, including international returns, repairs, replacements, cross-border transfers, and movements to and from third-party facilities.
* Establish consistent procedures for transaction screening, license verification, shipping documentation, customs clearance, and recordkeeping.
* Partner with Legal and Global Trade to apply export control and customs requirements to service transactions, including end-user, end-use, destination, and product eligibility reviews.
* Help service teams use accurate product classifications, country-of-origin information, and customs values for returned, repaired, refurbished, and replacement products.
* Build compliance checks into receiving, RMA processing, inventory transfers, outbound fulfillment, and disposition workflows.
Lead operational reviews, audits, and corrective actions to strengthen controls and prevent recurring issues.  

  

**What we need to see:**

* A bachelor’s degree in supply chain, international business, operations, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* 12+ years of relevant experience in trade compliance, customs, international logistics, or service supply chain operations, including 5+ years managing teams or complex programs.
* Understanding of RMA, repair, replacement, refurbishment, and service inventory procedures.
* Experience managing trade documentation, customs broker performance, shipment exceptions, and operational compliance controls.
The ability to translate regulatory mentorship into clear procedures, training, and system requirements.  

  

**Ways to stand out from the crowd:**

* Experience managing cross-border repair and return programs, including temporary imports and exports, duty relief, and returned-goods processes.
* Familiarity with SAP, SAP Global Trade Services, warehouse management, or transportation management systems.
Experience improving trade compliance across third-party warehouses, repair centers, and global service networks.
